about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Chengdu Sliced Pork Belly with Doubanjiang and Leek
recipes.summary: Thick slices of simmered pork belly stir-fried until curled and crisp-edged with leek, doubanjiang and fermented.
steps: Put the pork belly in a pot with the ginger, spring onion and enough water to cover. Bring to the boil, then simmer gently for 25 minutes until just tender when pierced with a skewer. Lift out and cool for 15 minutes so it slices cleanly.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and keep it covered.
Slice the cooled pork into 3mm slices. Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the pork for 4 minutes, turning, until the fat renders and the edges curl and brown.
Push the pork aside, add the doubanjiang and black beans and stir for 30 seconds until the oil turns red and fragrant. Add the garlic and toss through.
Add the leek, sugar and wine and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the leek is tender but still bright. Serve straight away over the rice.
notes: Food safety: simmer the pork until cooked through and keep leftovers refrigerated for no more than 2 days; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Sichuan. Dinner.

recipes.title: Cantonese Steamed Pork Patty with Mushrooms
recipes.summary: A tender hand-chopped style pork patty steamed with shiitake and ginger, with its own savoury juices spooned over rice.
steps: Soak the shiitake in hot water for 20 minutes until soft, then squeeze dry, remove the stems and chop finely.
Mix the pork with the shiitake, ginger, half the spring onion, soy sauce, oyster sauce, cornflour, sesame oil and sugar. Stir in one direction for 2 minutes until sticky and cohesive.
Press the mixture into a shallow heatproof dish in an even layer. Steam over boiling water for 15 minutes until the pork is cooked through and the juices run clear.
Meanwhile cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then steam the bok choy for 3 minutes until just tender.
Scatter the patty with the remaining spring onion and serve with the rice, bok choy and the juices from the dish.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork patty until no pink remains and the juices run clear; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Cantonese. Lunch.

recipes.title: Hakka Stuffed Tofu Puffs with Pork
recipes.summary: Hakka yong tau foo style: tofu puffs stuffed with a ginger pork filling, browned and braised in a light garlic soy.
steps: Mix the pork with the spring onion, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil and cornflour until sticky. Make a slit in each tofu puff and press in a spoonful of filling.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the stuffed puffs, filling side down, for 3 minutes each side until golden.
Add the garlic and stir for 20 seconds until fragrant, then pour in the stock and oyster sauce. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes until the pork is cooked through.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Blanch the gai lan for 2 minutes until bright green and tender.
Spoon the puffs and sauce over the rice and serve with the gai lan.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork filling until no pink remains in the centre of a puff; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Hakka. Dinner.

recipes.title: Okinawan Taco Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Okinawa's beloved taco rice: spiced beef mince over hot rice, topped with lettuce, tomato and melted cheddar.
steps: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and keep it warm.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and beef and brown for 6 minutes, breaking up the lumps, until no pink remains.
Stir in the taco seasoning, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce and water and simmer for 3 minutes until thick and glossy.
Divide the rice between 4 bowls and spoon over the beef. Top with the cheddar so it melts, then the lettuce and tomato.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef mince until browned right through with no pink remaining; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Okinawa. Lunch.

recipes.title: Miyazaki Chicken Nanban with Tartare Sauce
recipes.summary: Kyushu's crisp fried chicken dipped in a sweet vinegar glaze and finished with a creamy egg and pickle tartare.

items: 600g chicken thigh, cut in large pieces

steps: Hard-boil 1 egg for 9 minutes, cool, peel and mash with the mayonnaise, pickle and chives to make the tartare.
Stir the soy sauce, vinegar and sugar in a small pot over low heat for 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves, then pour into a shallow dish.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Dust the chicken in the flour, then dip in the remaining beaten egg.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 170C and fry the chicken in batches for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through. Drain briefly.
Turn each piece in the sweet vinegar glaze, slice and serve over the rice with the cabbage and tartare spooned over.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75C in the thickest part; eggs should be fully cooked; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Kyushu. Dinner.

recipes.title: Jeyuk Bokkeum Spicy Pork with Rice
recipes.summary: A fiery Korean pork stir-fry with gochujang, gochugaru and onion, served with rice and lettuce leaves for wrapping.
steps: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, garlic and ginger into a paste, then coat the pork in it.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.

Heat the oil in a wok or large pan over high heat and stir-fry the onion for 2 minutes until just softened. Add the pork in two batches and cook for 5 minutes each until browned with no pink remaining.
Return everything to the pan, toss with the spring onion for 1 minute until glossy, and serve over rice with lettuce leaves for wrapping.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork until browned right through and keep leftovers refrigerated; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Marinating the pork for 30 minutes gives deeper flavour. Dinner.

recipes.title: Isaan Crying Tiger Steak with Jaew Dipping Sauce
recipes.summary: Isaan-style grilled beef sliced and served with a smoky, tangy jaew sauce and sticky rice.
steps: Soak the sticky rice in water for 30 minutes if you have time, then steam it over boiling water for 25 minutes until tender and chewy.
Toast the rice flour in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes until golden and nutty, then tip out.
Brush the steak with the soy sauce and oil and cook in a hot pan or grill for 4 minutes each side for medium until well browned. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, chilli flakes, shallot, coriander, spring onion and toasted rice flour together until the sugar dissolves.
Serve the steak with the jaew sauce, sticky rice and cucumber.
notes: Food safety: cook beef steak to your preference but rest it, and keep the whole-muscle surface well seared; check the thickest part reaches 63°C for a steak.
Gluten-free if tamari is used for the soy sauce. Dinner.

recipes.title: Hue Banh Beo Steamed Rice Cakes with Prawn
recipes.summary: Hue's delicate steamed rice cakes in small dishes, topped with minced prawn, crisp shallots and a sweet fish sauce.
steps: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, 2 cups water, salt and oil until smooth. Lightly oil 16 small heatproof dishes or ramekins.
Set the dishes in a steamer over boiling water for 5 minutes to heat. Fill each halfway with batter and steam for 10 minutes until set translucent and springy.
Stir-fry the minced prawn in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until pink and cooked through. Add the spring onion for 30 seconds until wilted.
Stir the fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, chilli and 1/2 cup water until the sugar dissolves, to make the dressing.
Loosen each cake with a small spoon. Top with prawn and fried shallots and spoon over the dressing, serving warm.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawn until opaque and pink and eat the same day; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Hue. Dinner. Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Telur Balado Padang Eggs in Chilli Sambal
recipes.summary: West Sumatran Padang eggs fried until blistered and simmered in a spicy red chilli and tomato sambal, served with rice.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the eggs for 4 minutes, turning, until the skins blister and turn golden. Lift out.
Blend the chillies, shallot, garlic and tomato to a coarse paste. Fry in the remaining oil for 8 minutes until darkened and the oil separates.
Stir in the sugar, salt and lime juice, return the eggs and coat for 2 minutes until heated through.
Serve with the rice and spoon over the sambal.
notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until fully set and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Padang. Lunch. Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Nyonya Ayam Pongteh Braised Chicken
recipes.summary: A Melaka Nyonya braise of chicken and potato with fermented black beans and palm sugar, rich but not spicy.
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and fry the shallot and garlic for 4 minutes until golden and fragrant.
Add the black beans, palm sugar and dark soy and stir for 1 minute until bubbling.
Add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes, then pour in the water and add the potato. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the potato is tender.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Uncover the pot for the last 5 minutes if you want the sauce thicker.
Serve the chicken with the sauce over the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the juices run clear and it reaches 75C; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Nyonya. Dinner.

recipes.title: Visayan Pork Humba
recipes.summary: A Visayan braise of pork belly in soy, vinegar and brown sugar with star anise and bay, until sticky and tender.
steps: Brown the pork belly in the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until golden on all sides.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, garlic, bay, star anise, pepper and water. Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 55 minutes until the pork is fork-tender.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Uncover and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce reduces to a sticky glaze that coats the pork.
Serve the pork and sauce spooned over the rice.
notes: Food safety: simmer the pork until tender and cooked through; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Visayan. Dinner.

recipes.title: Kerala Beef Ularthiyathu Dry Roast
recipes.summary: Kerala's slow-cooked dry beef roast with coconut slivers, curry leaf and black pepper, fried to a dark, spicy finish.
steps: Put the beef in a pot with the ginger garlic paste, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder, 1 tsp salt and the water. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the beef is tender and the liquid has reduced to a thick coating.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the coconut for 3 minutes until golden. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Fry the onion in the same oil for 8 minutes until deep golden, then add the curry leaf and black pepper for 30 seconds until crackling.
Add the beef with its sauce and the garam masala and stir-fry over medium-high heat for 10 minutes until dark, dry and glossy. Fold in the toasted coconut.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and serve with the beef.
notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender and cooked through and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Kerala. Dinner. Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Goan Chicken Xacuti
recipes.summary: Goa's complex coconut and toasted spice curry, built on dry-roasted coriander, poppy-free spice paste and a hint of.

items: 900g chicken thigh, cut in large pieces

steps: Dry-roast the coconut in a pan over medium heat for 4 minutes until deep golden, then tip out. Roast the coriander, cumin, fennel, chilli, cinnamon, cloves and pepper for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Grind the roasted spices, coconut, half the onion and the garlic with 1/2 cup water to a smooth paste.
Fry the remaining onion in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the turmeric and the paste and cook for 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the chicken, tamarind, 1 tsp salt and the remaining water. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then serve with the curry.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the juices run clear and it reaches 75C; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Goa. Dinner. Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Bengali Shorshe Maach Mustard Fish Curry
recipes.summary: Bengal's pungent mustard fish: firm white fish in a sharp mustard seed and green chilli gravy cooked in mustard oil.

items: 600g white fish fillet, cut in large pieces

steps: Soak the mustard seed in 1/4 cup warm water for 10 minutes, then blend with 1 green chilli and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste.
Rub the fish with turmeric and salt. Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil in a pan until smoking, and sear the fish for 1 minute each side until just coloured, then lift out.
Add the remaining oil, cumin and the mustard paste and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add the water and 2 slit green chillies and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the fish and simmer gently for 6 minutes until opaque and cooked through.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and serve with the fish and gravy.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and eat the same day; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Bengal. Dinner. Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Samoan Sapasui Glass Noodles with Beef
recipes.summary: Samoan sapasui: slippery glass noodles stir-braised with beef, carrot, garlic and ginger in a soy sauce.
steps: Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 10 minutes until pliable, then drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the beef for 3 minutes until browned with no pink. Lift out.
Fry the onion, carrot, garlic and ginger for 3 minutes until fragrant and softened.
Add the stock, soy sauce and oyster sauce and bring to the boil, then add the noodles and toss for 4 minutes until they absorb the sauce and turn translucent.
Return the beef, fold in the spring onion for 1 minute until wilted, and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef through and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Samoa. Dinner.
